label: Dairy
examples: Milk, cheese, yogurt, ice cream, butter
watch_for: Lactose is the most common single trigger for gas, bloating and loose stool. Cow's milk protein can also reach a breastfed baby.

label: Wheat & gluten
watch_for: Bloating and cramping a few hours later; a long-running pattern is worth a doctor's visit rather than a guess.

label: Caffeine
examples: Coffee, espresso, tea, cola, energy drinks
watch_for: Speeds the gut up — looser, more urgent stool. Passes into breast milk and can keep a baby wakeful.

label: Alcohol
watch_for: Reflux and poor sleep. If breastfeeding, follow your provider's timing guidance.

label: Carbonated drinks
watch_for: Swallowed gas comes back out as burping and bloating, usually within the hour.

label: Spicy food
watch_for: Reflux and heartburn the same evening; looser stool the next morning.

label: Fried & fatty food
examples: Fried chicken, chips, pizza, creamy sauces
watch_for: Fat slows the stomach down — fullness, reflux, and a delayed, heavier bowel movement.

label: Beans & legumes
watch_for: Classic gas at 4–8 hours. Worth logging the portion, since small amounts are often fine.

label: Cruciferous vegetables
examples: Broccoli, cauliflower, cabbage, Brussels sprouts, kale
watch_for: Gas and bloating, often overnight.

label: Onion & garlic
watch_for: High-FODMAP; bloating and cramping for some people and nothing at all for others.

label: Artificial sweeteners
examples: Sugar-free gum, diet drinks, protein bars, sorbitol, xylitol
watch_for: Sugar alcohols draw water into the gut — urgent, loose stool at fairly small doses.

label: Citrus & acidic food
watch_for: Heartburn and reflux, usually within an hour or two.

label: Chocolate
watch_for: Relaxes the valve at the top of the stomach — reflux, especially lying down.

label: High-fiber food
examples: Whole grains, bran, berries, prunes, salad
watch_for: Usually helps regularity; a sudden increase causes gas and cramping for a few days.

label: Red meat
watch_for: Slower to move through; can firm stool up or delay it a day.

label: Processed & cured food
examples: Deli meat, bacon, sausage, instant noodles
watch_for: Salt and fat together; bloating and firmer stool.

label: Nuts & seeds
watch_for: Common allergen. Anything beyond digestive upset — swelling, hives, breathing trouble — is an emergency, not a log entry.

label: Eggs
watch_for: Common allergen; can also reach a breastfed baby.

label: Fish & shellfish
watch_for: Common allergen. Note the kind eaten — shellfish and fin fish are different triggers.

label: Water
watch_for: The one input worth logging for its absence. Low intake shows up as dark urine and hard stool.
